Anya R.: Quick heads-up — starting a short bakeoff for model-x quant variants (FP8, AWQ-4bit, GPTQ-int8). Goal: pick defaults for hosted vs dedicated and define canary/fallback heuristics. Need: accuracy delta vs fp16, hallucination rate, p50/p95 latency, and cost reduction estimates.
Sam K.: SGTM. Sequence: smoke on dedicated (isolated), then hosted staged rollout. Propose thresholds: <=1.5% accuracy drop, p95 latency <=1.3x baseline, tail latency increase cap 200ms, fallback budget 10% traffic.
Jin W.: Pushed initial eval results from the lab run (1k prompts each): AWQ-4bit -> accuracy -1.8%, hallucination +0.9%, p95 +120ms, cost ~3.2x reduction. GPTQ-int8 -> accuracy -0.9%, hallucination +0.3%, p95 +80ms, cost ~2.1x. FP8 -> accuracy -0.6%, hallucination +0.2%, p95 +150ms, cost ~2.8x. Raw artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bakeoffs/model-x/182345.
Liam P.: OK — AWQ gives biggest cost wins but notable quality delta. For hosted defaults, leaning GPTQ-int8 (better quality/latency). For Dedicated we can offer AWQ as a performance tier behind an opt-in config.
Anya R.: We need concrete rollout rules. Draft: Dedicated: deploy to reserved pools only after gated A/B run (10% traffic for 48h). Fail fast if accuracy drift >1.0% absolute or error-rate +0.2% vs baseline. Hosted: staged "traffic corridor": 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 7 days with golden-set checks at each step. Fallback: immediate routing to fp16 variant + page on fail.
Sam K.: How do we detect "accuracy drift" in production? Use a golden prompt set + rolling sampling. Compute exact-match, rouge-l, and bertscore on 1k sampled prompts every 6h. If any metric crosses its threshold we trigger a circuit.
Jin W.: Implementation caveats: KV-cache behavior differs across quant implementations. AWQ requires a cache warm-up policy to avoid initial response mismatch for long-context flows. During canary pin the seq-len distribution to typical app patterns. Also ensure deterministic naming: model-x-awq-1.0, model-x-gptq-1.0, model-x-fp8-1.0.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: model-x-gptq-1.0 on hosted-us-east-1 (0.5% traffic). Link: https://console.redwood/models/model-x/gptq/rollouts/182345
Liam P.: If canary passes, auto-advance after 24h of no regressions. For dedicated, keep canary window at 48h. Also add a "gradual CPU backoff" when oversubscription hits — prevents queue pileups on private installs.
Jin W.: Suggested alert rule (pseudo):
```
WHEN golden_accuracy_drop > 0.8% FOR 2 consecutive windows(6h)
OR p95_latency_increase > 1.25x
THEN route_100%_to(fallback=fp16) AND create_incident(sev=2)
```
Anya R.: OK I'll turn this into a proper runbook and rollout YAML. Action items: Jin -> attach full evaluation artifacts and KV-cache notes; Sam -> produce hosted rollout config + thresholds; Liam -> dedicated pool policy and opt-in docs. Ping me here when done. :thumbsup:
Sam K.: I'll start the hosted rollout config today and post the PR.
Jin W.: Uploading the AWQ tuning logs now. Will also add a small prompt set that highlights hallucination regressions.
Anya R.: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after the first hosted canary completes.
